A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Morph research work, including all 16 pages, Tables 1–9, Figures 1–7, and Appendices A–H. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original motion-generation experiments on HumanML3D and AIST++, component ablations, supplementary generalization experiments, and a user study.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix analyses and user study.

M1.justification: The motion generator, physics refinement module, prior reward, imitation selection, and collaborative training and inference procedures are unchanged in Section 3 and the appendix.

E1.justification: Both versions retain HumanML3D and AIST++ evaluations and the same supplementary cross-task, action-conditioned, and long-duration dance scenarios in Table 9.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in every corresponding experiment, including PhysDiff and Reindiffuse in Table 2, FACT and TM2D in Table 4, and the PHC comparison in Table 9.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 and the appendices retain identical dataset splits, preprocessing, metrics, training settings, thresholds, and evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The component ablations, threshold and data-quantity analyses, multi-round training experiments, semantic alignment analysis, generalization tests, and qualitative cases are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical: the same point estimates and user-study win rates appear, without added run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are identical, including Tables 1–9 and the appendix figures. For example, Table 2 retains Morph-MoMask FID 0.041, RTOP-3 0.816, and Float 2.141.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, MDP formulation, and Equations 1–6 are identical. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about motion-free, model-agnostic refinement, collaborative optimization, and improved physical plausibility with competitive generation quality.

C2.justification: The interpretations of reward effects, domain gaps, semantic alignment, and generalization are unchanged, as are the stated limitations concerning interactive and non-grounded motions.

D1.justification: v4 adds a project-page hyperlink to the abstract that v3 lacks. Implementation and preprocessing details remain identical; the PDFs do not establish that code or data have been released through the linked page.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to earlier physics-based motion methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds a short project-page pointer and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining wording and section organization, including the appendices, are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added hyperlink slightly reflows the first-page abstract. Figures, tables, captions, and their placement are unchanged; rendered pages 2–16 are identical.

improvement.justification: The new abstract hyperlink offers a small reader-access benefit by providing a direct project-page pointer absent from v3. Scientific content and evidential quality are unchanged, and the PDFs do not verify the linked page's contents or resource availability.
